Implements steps 1-3 of discussion #644: https://github.com/qelectrotech/qelectrotech-source-mirror/discussions/644

That discussion proposes a much larger bounded-diagnostic-log design (crash-safe ring flush, signal handlers, diagnostics export UI). It explicitly splits into 5 independently-shippable steps of increasing risk and says step 1 is "worth merging regardless of whether the rest ever gets built." This PR is steps 1-3 only, by design — see "Deliberately not included" below.

## Step 1 — fix the existing logger (bugs, no new behavior)

- One `QFile` handle held open for the whole session under a mutex, instead of opening and closing the log file on **every single message** (the discussion cites a burst of ~140 identical warnings in #635 as 140 full open/close cycles).
- The log directory and the session's date-stamped filename are resolved **exactly once**, in the new `QetLogger::init()` called explicitly from `main()` immediately before `qInstallMessageHandler()` — not recomputed per message, so a session that runs past midnight now stays in one file instead of silently splitting.
- Age-based retention now uses `lastModified()` instead of `lastRead()` — opening a log to attach it to a bug report no longer resets its retention clock and keeps it alive indefinitely.
- stderr and file output both encode UTF-8 explicitly, replacing stderr's `toLocal8Bit()` (lossy for CJK/Cyrillic project paths) and the file stream's previously Qt5/Qt6-inconsistent default encoding.

## Step 2 — size-capped rotation + hardening

- The previously-unbounded daily file is now capped at 2 MiB and rotated, keeping `<date>.log` plus `<date>.1.log` .. `<date>.4.log`; oldest dropped.
- Each message is truncated to 4 KB with a marker before it reaches the ring or the file.
- Control characters in message content are escaped — much of what QET logs is externally controlled (file paths, element names, font strings out of a `.qet` file), and left unescaped an embedded `\n` could forge log lines.
- The log file is refused if a symlink already exists at that path, and is created/rotated owner-read/write only (0600).

## Step 3 — in-memory ring buffer

`LogRing` is a fixed-capacity, always-on ring of the last 4096 log lines, preallocated once at construction (4096 × 512 B = 2 MiB) so `append()` never allocates. Entries are stored as plain pre-formatted bytes in fixed-size slots — the shape the discussion specifies so a *future* crash handler could dump it with nothing but `write(2)`, even though no such handler exists yet. Thread-safe via a plain `QMutex` — the lock-free requirement in the discussion applies specifically to a signal-handler read path, which this step doesn't add.

## Escape hatch

`QET_LOG_DISABLE=1` in the environment at startup bypasses all of the above — no ring, no file, no rotation — falling back to a minimal, self-contained stderr passthrough that shares no code with the new formatting/sanitization path, so it stays usable even if that path is what's misbehaving.

## Deliberately not included, per the discussion's own phasing

- **No signal handler / crash-time ring flush (step 4)** — the discussion itself flags this as the highest-risk piece ("lands last, behind its own switch"), needing `sigaltstack`, async-signal-safety throughout, and careful interaction with core dumps. Not attempted here.
- **No diagnostics export UI (step 5)**.
- No log categories, session header, repeat collapsing or rate limiting — listed under "best practices worth building in" in the discussion, not part of steps 1-3.

## Testing

Built clean, no new warnings.

Verified with real runs (`QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`, isolated `HOME`):
- Log file created at the expected `dataDir()/YYYYMMDD.log` path, mode 0600.
- A full startup's worth of real messages (translation loading, `MachineInfo`'s system dump, collection loading) written correctly; every line of a 231-line run starts with a proper timestamp — confirmed the sanitizer correctly escapes the raw embedded newlines/tabs in `MachineInfo`'s multi-line CPU/GPU description fields into visible `\n`/`\t` sequences instead of letting them fragment the log into extra lines.
- `QET_LOG_DISABLE=1`: zero log files created, stderr still worked via the independent legacy path.
- Rotation: pre-filled a log to just under the 2 MiB cap, ran a normal session, confirmed it rotated to `<date>.1.log` (still 0600) with a byte-clean split — no truncated or duplicated line at the boundary — and a fresh `<date>.log` picked up cleanly from the next message.
